question: What is the primary reason drug absorption is slow via the subcutaneous route?

options.A: Low local temperature slows down fluid movement
options.B: Subcutaneous fat actively repels fluid medications
options.C: The tissue layer has a sparse blood supply
options.D: The skin barrier blocks rapid chemical uptake

explanation: The limited number of blood vessels in subcutaneous tissue restricts how fast medication enters the systemic circulation. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T7#GNS125_U3_T7_h1)

question: A patient with very low body fat requires a subcutaneous injection. What adjustment should the nurse anticipate?

options.A: Switching the medication route entirely to intravenous
options.B: Using a longer needle at a perpendicular angle
options.C: Injecting deeper into the underlying muscle tissue
options.D: Pinching the skin and using a shorter or angled needle

explanation: Thin patients lack deep subcutaneous fat, requiring skin bunching and shallow angles to avoid accidental intramuscular delivery. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T7#GNS125_U3_T7_h1)

question: What is the maximum safe fluid volume usually recommended for a single subcutaneous injection in adults?
explanation: Exceeding small volumes in the subcutaneous space causes excessive pressure, severe pain, and potential tissue damage. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T7#GNS125_U3_T7_h2)

question: Why are large fluid volumes avoided when giving medications into the subcutaneous tissue?

options.A: It causes painful pressure and localized tissue damage
options.B: It forces the medication directly into the bloodstream
options.C: It immediately precipitates an acute allergic reaction
options.D: It neutralizes the pharmacological effect of the drug

explanation: The tight connective matrix cannot expand easily, meaning large fluid amounts create pressure and ischemia. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T7#GNS125_U3_T7_h2)

question: Which body area generally provides the most rapid and consistent absorption for subcutaneous insulin?
explanation: Abdominal subcutaneous fat has high blood perfusion compared to limbs, leading to faster insulin uptake. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T7#GNS125_U3_T7_h3)

question: A nurse prepares to give a routine subcutaneous injection to an adult. Which needle size is most appropriate?
explanation: A fine gauge (25 to 30) and short length (3/8 to 5/8 inch) target the subcutaneous layer while minimizing patient discomfort. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T7#GNS125_U3_T7_h3)

question: What is the correct action regarding skin preparation before inserting a subcutaneous needle?

options.A: Massage the antiseptic vigorously into the skin layers
options.B: Blow on the wet antiseptic site to dry it quickly
options.C: Allow the alcohol swab cleanser to dry completely
options.D: Apply ice immediately after cleaning to numb the area

explanation: Allowing the alcohol to dry ensures its antimicrobial action works and prevents wet alcohol from stinging as the needle enters. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T7#GNS125_U3_T7_h4)

question: Why should the nurse avoid massaging the injection site after administering certain subcutaneous drugs like heparin?

options.A: Friction neutralizes the chemical structure of the active drug
options.B: It forces the fluid directly into the underlying bone matrix
options.C: It pushes the medication backward out through the puncture hole
options.D: Massage causes local trauma, bruising, and rapid drug dispersion

explanation: Friction damages fragile capillaries in the subcutaneous tissue, leading to hematoma formation and erratic drug absorption rates. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T7#GNS125_U3_T7_h4)

question: What complication occurs when a patient repeatedly uses the exact same subcutaneous injection site?
explanation: Continuous insulin exposure in one spot stimulates local fat growth, forming rubbery lumps known as lipohypertrophy. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T7#GNS125_U3_T7_h5)

question: Why is systematic site rotation clinically necessary for patients receiving daily subcutaneous injections?

options.A: It maintains predictable drug absorption and prevents tissue damage
options.B: It completely eliminates the sensation of pain during insertion
options.C: It stops the immune system from developing systemic allergies
options.D: It prevents the needle from becoming dull during repeated use

explanation: Healthy, undamaged tissue ensures proper drug uptake, whereas scarred or fatty tissue alters pharmacokinetics. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T7#GNS125_U3_T7_h5)
